topic: The story of how James Dyson invented the bagless vacuum cleaner and built a $20 billion company despite repeated rejections.

script: In 1979, James Dyson bought a vacuum cleaner and immediately noticed it lost suction. He took it apart and found the bag clogged with dust, the very thing it was supposed to collect. He was convinced there was a better way. He built a prototype using cardboard and tape. It worked, so he spent the next 5 years building 5,127 prototypes in the shed behind his house, running out of money, borrowing against everything he owned. Then he tried to sell it. Hoover turned him down—they made too much money selling replacement bags to ever want a bagless vacuum. Electrolux told him it was impossible. Every major manufacturer said no. He eventually licensed it to a Japanese company, used the royalties to set up his own factory, and launched the DC01 in the UK in 1993. It became Britain's best-selling vacuum cleaner within two years. Then came bladeless fans, hand dryers, and a hair dryer that changed the beauty industry. James Dyson's net worth is over 20 billion dollars today.
retention_tricks: animated counters for prototype attempts and net worth
funny stick-figure animations combined with real photo cutouts
what_makes_it_work: Combined simple stick figure animation with real product images to make a historical story fun and visually dynamic.
Utilized animated numbers (5,127 prototypes and $20B net worth) to visually emphasize struggle and immense triumph.
Framed the story around dramatic conflict: extreme industry rejection turning into ultimate market dominance.
